ladder_cells_CURVE-J12S1_m2_ten_cells.why_this_ladder: A DOUBLING LADDER WITH A MATCHED +1 COMPANION AT EVERY RUNG. The doubling gives a sixteen-fold range of B at a FIXED curve, which is the independence-of-B lever. The +1 companion gives the residue contrast: _build_phi_invariant_factor_base returns xs[:B], so at B = 3q+1 the LAST phi-orbit is TRUNCATED to a single element whose phi-image is not in F, while at B = 3q the factor base is a clean union of q whole orbits. B mod 3 is therefore the one structural variable that separates a phi-invariant factor base from an almost-phi-invariant one, and it is varied at every rung rather than confounded with size.
